analysis: Bonferroni and Holm-Bonferroni correction for the spectral pruning campaign
family: All 4 permutation-based correlation tests in the campaign (Exps 29-42)

Exp 32 (lmin~importance@square).note: The direction was ALREADY refuted by Exp 41 real-pruning. The correlation exists but is superseded by the direct test.

Exp 33a (pythia-410 criterion).note: Never was significant. The signal at square point is zero in fully-collapsed models.

Exp 34 H2 (lmin head-stable across T).note: SURVIVES. The head-stability of the collapse signature is robust.

Exp 34 H3 (sub-square predicts importanc.note: Does not survive at the Bonferroni threshold. However, the direction was confirmed by Exp 34b real-pruning (ascending: 65k vs random: 114k). The correlation is suggestive; the direct test is the evidence.

holm_bonferroni.verdict: Only H2 survives the Holm-Bonferroni step-down.

implications_for_paper: 1) The correlation-based claims (Exp 32, Exp 34 H3) are demoted from 'confirmed' to 'suggestive'. They do NOT survive multiple-comparison correction at alpha=0.05/4.
2) The head-stability finding (H2) survives and is upgraded: it is the ONLY correlation test that survives Bonferroni.

3) The primary claims are NOT affected: they are effect-size driven, not p-value driven. Exp 41/V41 (pruning direction, ppl 67x separation) and Exp 42 (benchmark, spec 166 vs michel 251) are direct interventional tests, not correlations. Bonferroni does not apply to them.
4) Exp 34b (real pruning at sub-square) supersedes the Exp 34 H3 correlation as the evidence for sub-square signal.
5) The paper must report the corrected alpha and state which tests survive. This is what a careful reviewer will demand.
honest_label: We ran 4 correlation tests across the campaign. After Bonferroni, only 1 survives. The paper's primary claims rest on interventional effect sizes (not p-values), but the supporting correlations are weaker than initially reported. This correction strengthens the paper's credibility.
